newsitem.title: UK: Euro stocks dip on Greenspan warning, dollar up.
newsitem.headline: Euro stocks dip on Greenspan warning, dollar up.

text.p: European bourses dipped on Wednesday as U.S. central bank chief Alan Greenspan voiced concerns about soaring stock prices but his hints about a rise in interest rates boosted the dollar.
Shares in London, Frankfurt and Paris, which had been marking time ahead of the keynote speech, tumbled minutes after Greenspan spoke before recovering some poise.
But his words had the opposite effect on currency markets where the dollar rose sharply as dealers interpreted them as a hint that U.S. interest rates will be raised to nip inflation in the bud.
Although Greenspan delivered a largely upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy his worries about stock prices and the risk of higher inflation unnerved the markets on both sides of the Atlantic.

The Dow Jones industrial average was hit harder than European bourses, which regained most of the lost ground. The Dow fell about 1.5 percent and was still showing a loss of 1.0 percent at the European close.
"Even I must admit that our economic prospects in general are quite favourable," Greenspan said in his semiannual economic testimony to Congress.
But investors took fright as Greenspan warned that financial markets, including investors in stocks and junk bonds, may be over-optimistic about the economic outlook and urged caution.
"Such caution seems especially warranted with regard to the sharp rise in equity prices during the past two years," he said. "These gains have obviously raised questions of sustainability."
Greenspan credited much of the economy's recent good performance to the low rate of inflation, but said that may not last.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, slipped quickly by 0.5 percent as Greenspan's remarks cast gloom over the market. London and other bourses in Europe have been trading at record levels in recent weeks.
Most European investors were rattled by the prospect of inflationary pressure pushing up interest rates in the U.S. economy which will impact on the rest of the world.
"Greenspan. That sums up the Dow slide in a word," said Hildegard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities, in New York.
"This time he is not hedging. He wants to talk the market down. He is saying we are not in a new era, we should use caution and that there is a possibility of a rate rise if stocks keep going up."
But London regained some of the lost ground to show a loss of only 0.35 percent at the close.

Wednesday's fall was a blip compared to the reaction to Greenspan's remarks last December about "irrational exuberance" in U.S. asset markets, which caused a temporary nose-dive in stocks on both sides of the Atlantic.
In Paris, shares fell 0.4 percent on the strength of Greenspan's warning but climbed back and ended the day only a few points down.
Frankfurt fell initially in computerised trade but managed to haul itself into the plus column by the close. Floor trade which ended before Greenspan spoke finished up a few points.
On currency markets, the dollar strengthened as dealers saw prospects for higher interest rates as good news for the U.S. currency, making it more attractive to investors.
"The dollar got a boost because the market took his comments as implying that U.S. rates will go up soon," said Michael O'Hanlon, chief international economist at Paine Webber.
He added that he expected to dollar to maintain its upward bias in the run-up to the next meeting of the FOMC policy-making committee of U.S. central bank.
"The dollar should be well supported on dips as Greenspan's comments appear to have raised the chances of a rate hike, possibly in March, or at least in the first half of this year."
By the close of European trade, the dollar had recovered most of its losses after dropping by nearly two yen and half a pfennig as dealers grew jittery ahead of the testimony.
The U.S. currency ended up one pfennig on Tuesday's closing levels and, against the yen, closed little different from last night's European rate.
CURRENCIES AT 1700
The dollar was quoted at 1.6892 marks and 122.23 yen, compared with 1.6786 and 122.24 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 15.4 points at 4,329.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed 5.55 points down at 2,602.17.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index finished up 4.66 points at 3,237.87.
PRECIOUS METALS
GOLD closed at $353.85 compared with $353.35 at the London close on Tuesday. Silver was up two cents at $5.23 in late trade.
